reason: Both correctly routed the homeowner to the consumer unit rather than the plug and both identified the Fairy liquid as the cause, but Conversation 1 handled the live emergency far better: it gave ordered, calm instructions, addressed the extension lead specifically, asked the right narrowing questions, and then delivered a complete recovery plan (scoop foam, oil/vinegar, detergent-free rinse cycles, clean filter, inform landlord with photos) with proportionate escalation only if the socket actually got wet. Conversation 2 asserted as fact that water had 'reached your plug sockets' when it hadn't (socket is at worktop height), answered 'Yes' to 'should i just pull the plug' before clarifying, told them to inspect seals and hoses before asking what was happening, and ended with an unsupported demand that an engineer inspect the appliance while offering no advice at all on clearing the suds or getting the machine working again. Conversation 1 also correctly recognised that no part or engineer was needed for the dishwasher itself.
